correctness.rationale: The frozen fixed-target quantifier includes H={0}, for which every signal vanishes and the inequality holds at every n; its sharpness statement also fails in that target. It therefore cannot pass literally. The complete corrected RESULT.md under /workspace/repairs/3 specifies nonzero H for both directions and states the trivial space separately; the verification note and slogan are synchronized there. For the corrected claim, integrating t exp(−(lambda+mu)t) gives the real cross coefficient a=lambda*mu/(lambda+mu)^2 and the diagonal coefficient 1/4. Difference of the two squared quadratics yields 4(1−4a)s[A+(1+4a)sB+s²C], with A=sum u³v, B=sum u²v² and C=sum uv³. Since 1−4a=(lambda−mu)^2/(lambda+mu)^2>0, any nonzero A suffices for a sign-changing perturbation. On C_n for n≥5, mode 3 is not 0 or ±1 modulo n, hence has distinct positive eigenvalue from mode 1 even at the smallest aliasing orders. The triple-angle identity makes A=||v||²_2/4≥n/8, with ||v||²_2=n at n=6 and n/2 otherwise. The bracket for s=−1/64 stays above n(1/8−2/64−1/4096)>0. A real scalar witness embeds on a unit line of each nonzero real or complex H. At n=3 there is only one nonzero eigenvalue. At n=4, antipodal parity of the eigenvalue-four and eigenvalue-two components cancels sum q_j c_j, with rho=8/9, leaving (17/81)sum c_j². This proves the equality condition using real inner products even for complex H, and pure nonzero modes prove sharpness in the two contracting cases.
residual_risks: Independent exact sample arithmetic is reproducible from the explicit C_6 and complex C_4 vectors in the replacement VERIFICATION.md; deficits are −20493/640000 and 136/81, respectively. The uniform Fourier argument, not those finite replays or the frozen floating-point checks, establishes the all-n statement. No optimal constant for n≥5 or general necessity of the cubic criterion is asserted.

evidence: Lai–Li–Li give bounds for the same temporal functional over all symmetric submarkovian semigroups and the exact half normalization at spatial p=2. Their quoted general bound at p=4 is not 1/2 and their sharpness lower comparisons concern Euclidean heat and dimension. Feneuil uses fractional powers of I−P and powers of a discrete Markov operator P on a weighted graph.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A bound holding on all symmetric semigroups with a nonsharp p=4 factor does not decide if the half benchmark fails on a particular cycle. Discrete-time bounds do not give the normalized continuous-time obstruction, and complete bipartiteness only covers one of the tested cycles.

At K_{2,2}, the complete-bipartite result gives rho_A=rho_B=8/9 and equality when each within-part contrast is real-orthogonal to its between-part value. The parts are the opposite vertex pairs, so the identity is exactly the C_4 deficit after writing c_j=2 Re inner product. The failing complete-bipartite example uses a cubic imbalance on a size-three part.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: C_4 and its orthogonality equality criterion are direct previous specializations, and the cubic mechanism has a concrete special-case precedent. But C_n for n≥5 is not complete bipartite and the earlier P_4 example is not a cycle. To get the general sufficient criterion one must retain the first variation A of the mixed-mode deficit; to get the cycle result one must then establish A≥n/8 and bound the higher terms uniformly. Those implications are not supplied by either inspected graph-family proof.

originality.rationale: For the repaired claim, the pointwise kernel, factor 1/2 for single eigenmodes, scalar triangle and the four-cycle result including its Hilbert-valued equality criterion are already supplied by known background and overlapping graph results. The replacement credits them explicitly. The surviving contribution on the available evidence is the uniform analytic failure theorem with the same explicit witness on every longer cycle and the general eigenspace-cubic sufficient criterion. This is a limited literature assessment, not a priority attestation.
residual_risks: An older perturbative theorem for pointwise spectral-multiplier kernels or temporal fourth moments could give the general sufficient obstruction. The tested web and corpus searches do not certify historical absence. Dungey's directly cited publisher PDF was not readable via that route; the space-gradient distinction is also identified in Feneuil's introduction.

value.rationale: The half coefficient is forced by pure heat modes, so it is mathematically meaningful to distinguish when mixing modes forces a larger constant. The repaired result exhibits the same bounded-size Fourier prescription at every longer cycle and isolates a reusable signed test for spectral mixing, treating the two small contracting cases as established calibrations rather than new discoveries. It is not a numerical norm table or a trivial consequence of replacing the zero target by a nonzero one.
residual_risks: This assessment is for the half-benchmark, not the exact best constants of failing cycles or an all-graph classification.
